purpose: Replace the full 18-state C4 colouring surface by the exact 12-state exposed quotient for decision, then derive and exhaustively cross-check the global F3 Fourier-current contraction used by the constructive solver path.

decision_quotient.fiber_profile: six exposed states have two full lifts and six have one full lift
decision_quotient.wire_map: F18 descends exactly to T on exposed states
decision_quotient.splice_congruence: Every physical exposed-port NEQ predicate is constant on full-state fibers. Hence every quotient solution lifts by choosing arbitrary full lifts at wire inputs and propagating them with F18.
decision_quotient.consequence: For arbitrary compositions built only from the canonical wire map and exposed-port NEQ splices, satisfiability of the 12-state quotient is equivalent to satisfiability of the full 18-state network. Multiplicity is irrelevant for decision.

local_fourier.wire_state_parameterization: x(c,s,q)=c*1+s*v_q over F3, c in F3, s in {+1,-1}, q in {+1,-1}
local_fourier.wire_transform: W_hat(k)=0 unless sum_i k_i=0; on that conservation hyperplane W_hat(k)=3*(h(k.v_plus)+h(k.v_minus))

global_closed_network_theorem.setting: A closed network with m canonical six-port quotient wires and a perfect matching of all 6m exposed ports into 3m NEQ3 splice edges.
global_closed_network_theorem.notation: Orient each splice edge and assign one current k_e in F3. At each wire v, pull the incident edge currents back to the canonical six-port order with signs induced by edge orientation. Let K be the set of current assignments satisfying the wire conservation equation sum_i k_{v,i}=0 for every wire. Define A_v(k)=h(k_v.v_plus)+h(k_v.v_minus).
global_closed_network_theorem.identity: Z = 3^(-2m) * sum_{k in K} [ product_e h(k_e) ] [ product_v A_v(k) ]
global_closed_network_theorem.decision_equivalence: Z is the nonnegative integer number of quotient assignments, so the original full-state network is satisfiable iff the current sum is nonzero.
global_closed_network_theorem.normalization_derivation: Unnormalized F3 Fourier inversion contributes 3^(-6m) from wire tensors and 3^(-6m) from 3m binary NEQ tensors; summing the 6m primal port variables contributes 3^(6m); eliminating edge dual variables contributes 3^(3m) from NEQ transforms and 3^m from wire transforms, leaving 3^(-2m).

exhaustive_global_control.method: For every permutation matching all six ports of wire 1 to all six ports of wire 2, compare direct enumeration over 12^2 quotient state pairs with the exact current sum over 3^6 edge-frequency assignments.

constructive_significance.completed_arrow: full C4 state network -> exact decision-preserving 12-state quotient -> exact F3 current contraction
constructive_significance.remaining_algorithmic_target: Evaluate or nonzero-test the global current sum in polynomial time without expanding exponentially many currents or transition choices, while retaining witness reconstruction.
constructive_significance.candidate_structure: Expand h(t)=3*delta[t=0]-1 and A_v=3*delta[l_plus=0]+3*delta[l_minus=0]-2. This converts the current contraction into a rank-generating state sum of linear F3 constraints, suggesting a weighted transition/interlace/multimatroid representation. Any claimed compression must prove that this state sum can be evaluated in polynomial time on the hard source.

external_context.hard_source: Fleischner-Sabidussi: 3-colourability remains NP-complete for 4-regular Hamiltonian graphs whose complementary cycles are non-selfcrossing cycles of fixed length at least four.
external_context.transition_machinery: Transition and interlace polynomials encode state sums of transitions/circuit partitions of 4-regular graphs; their general exact evaluations are often hard, so identifying our precise weighted specialization is mandatory before claiming a polynomial contraction.
